values.note: Forest Service dispersed camping: no reservations. 'Dispersed camping in one location is allowable up to 14 days in any 30-day period.' Not allowed near developed sites (campgrounds, picnic areas, trailheads); keep the campsite within 150 ft of the road.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/camping-cabins ('Recreationist can camp anywhere in the National Forest outside a designated campground'; 'Dispersed camping in one location is allowable up to 14 days in any 30-day period'; 'Dispersed camping is not allowed in the vicinity of developed recreation areas such as campgrounds, picnic areas, or trailheads ... Keep your campsite within 150 feet from a roadway'), read 2026-10-21

summary: No Forest Service page names this spot; confirmed from the GW&J forest's dispersed-camping rules: first-come, no reservations, 14 days in any 30 (overrides the inherited recreation.gov booking). Free fees left as recorded (manual). Not stated: season, facilities. Note left as is.
flags: Access criteria (AWH 2026-10-21 4WD rule, human decides): Virginia DWR's own Flagpole Knob page (https://dwr.virginia.gov/vbwt/sites/flagpole-knob/, read 2026-10-21) says 'Forest Service Road 85 towards the Flagpole Knob summit is remote, narrow, very steep, deeply rutted, and rocky. Only experienced overlanding/off-roading drivers should attempt this road.' and advises 'Park off the road at Briery Branch Gap ... and hike or mountain bike to the summit.' It does not say '4WD' in words, but it is an agency statement that the access road is for off-road vehicles/drivers; EKKO is not 4WD. This site is about 0.5 mi up that road from Briery Branch Gap (same road as Flagpole Knob id 403, flagged in p3-22). The Forest Service pages name no road condition.

Phone (info): 540-432-0187 is the North River Ranger District; its page says 'Phones are currently down as of 12/10/25 - Please email for questions' (brittany.lonas@usda.gov) and lists the Supervisor's Office, 540-265-5100.
